events.credibility_reason: No engagement in about 11 years on a landmark claim; the author replaced the argument in 2025; it reduces to metric-compatible connections, which is exactly where the known obstacle lies.
The authors withdrew the claim in v3 (Sep 2017): 'An error in the previous version was found' and 'The Chern conjecture remains open'.
Withdrawn by the author in v2 (Jul 2020), which names an error in Lemma 2.1 and another in a commutation of limits.

Several F10 signals together: no uptake on a landmark claim (and none for the 11-year-old line of argument it continues); Wikipedia still calls the problem open and does not cite it; nine revisions in eight months after a 10-year dormancy, with changes of title and route; the v12 abstract hedges ('We explore an approach') while the introduction claims a proof; the route goes through metric-compatible connections, which is the obstruction the problem is known to resist; and the author's own earlier general claim on this arXiv number was abandoned.
events.ai_basis: We are thankful to DeepSeek Chat (DeepSeek, 2024) for assistance with technical calculations related to the local metrizability of our 1-1-parameter family of connections.

events.credibility_reason: It rests on the author's own earlier Theorem 2.3, which belongs to the unreviewed and doubtful general-proof line; the author presents it as 'evidence' rather than a proof.

why: The statement is a single universal claim, so any proper subclass (Hessian, special, complete, amenable holonomy) is a case. Liu's compact-Hessian result is the cleanest post-snapshot case: credible but unreviewed. The researcher suggested it might be mere 'instances', but it proves the claim for an infinite class, which makes it a case. Casali-Moraschini proves a different quantity (simplicial volume) in the complete case, which was already settled, so it is a variant. The close call is Cocos 2025. It treats the whole problem and is unreviewed. I set it aside as not_credible rather than doubtful because the F10 signals arrive together: no uptake, many rapid revisions after a long dormancy, a hedged abstract, a method aimed at the known obstruction, and the author's abandoned 2015 argument. I dated it after the snapshot as a separate event because the record says the route changed in v4. Its DeepSeek credit covers 'technical calculations' on the key local-metrizability step. That is computation entering the argument, so I scored it assisted, but the evidence is thin. Older pre-snapshot classical results are marked digested as long-accepted literature.
doubts: The AI role on cocos-2025-revised-route is a close call between assisted and none: the calculations are not described, and the tail of the quote was not confirmed character by character. The not_credible call could reasonably be doubtful; it is the event's credibility, not its scope, that removes it. Many of the pre-snapshot classical events are known only from Wikipedia and secondary summaries; I marked them digested as established literature.
